"87a66aa8-c496-599b-ab47-b5f71305a74d" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{2}{\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "87a66aa8-c496-599b-ab47-b5f71305a74d" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}=3\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{3})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=3\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{2}{3}\cdot 3=2$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{x}{3} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "87a66aa8-c496-599b-ab47-b5f71305a74d" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "87a66aa8-c496-599b-ab47-b5f71305a74d" :question/answer-fields Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "9b712a6e-6e52-5783-8e96-8c4185897b37" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}=3\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{3})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=3\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{4}{3}\cdot 3=4$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=4\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
4\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=4\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
4\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{x}{3} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "9b712a6e-6e52-5783-8e96-8c4185897b37" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "9b712a6e-6e52-5783-8e96-8c4185897b37" :question/answer-fields Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "f0d24e1a-b76a-52fa-be50-ddfb085b96e6" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}=2\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{2})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=2\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $1\cdot 2=2$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "f0d24e1a-b76a-52fa-be50-ddfb085b96e6" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "f0d24e1a-b76a-52fa-be50-ddfb085b96e6" :question/answer-fields "3142b06d-bcb6-5c1e-8833-2865ec0d326e" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{3}{\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "3142b06d-bcb6-5c1e-8833-2865ec0d326e" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}=2\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{2})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=2\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{3}{2}\cdot 2=3$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=3\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
3\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=3\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
3\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "3142b06d-bcb6-5c1e-8833-2865ec0d326e" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "3142b06d-bcb6-5c1e-8833-2865ec0d326e" :question/answer-fields "ffa9d174-c2fd-5424-b8d2-3acccef9ad99" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{2}{\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "ffa9d174-c2fd-5424-b8d2-3acccef9ad99" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{4}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{4})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}=4\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{4})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=4\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4=2$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{x}{4} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "ffa9d174-c2fd-5424-b8d2-3acccef9ad99" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "ffa9d174-c2fd-5424-b8d2-3acccef9ad99" :question/answer-fields $$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\arcsin{\left(\frac{4 x}{3} \right)}+C.

"bae20d5d-4436-5e8e-8143-212aaf8c29ca" :question/id #uuid "bae20d5d-4436-5e8e-8143-212aaf8c29ca"] [:db/add "bae20d5d-4436-5e8e-8143-212aaf8c29ca" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - 9 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "bae20d5d-4436-5e8e-8143-212aaf8c29ca" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{3 x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{3}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{4 - 9 x^{2}}=2\sqrt{1-(\frac{3 x}{2})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{2}{3}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{3}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - 9 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{3}\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{3 x}{2} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "bae20d5d-4436-5e8e-8143-212aaf8c29ca" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "bae20d5d-4436-5e8e-8143-212aaf8c29ca" :question/answer-fields Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{25 - 16 x^{2}}=5\sqrt{1-(\frac{4 x}{5})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{5}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{2}{5}\cdot \frac{5}{4}=\frac{1}{2}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{\sqrt{25 - 16 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{2}\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{4 x}{5} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "5a421a58-948e-5542-a6c4-c105fa219eee" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "5a421a58-948e-5542-a6c4-c105fa219eee" :question/answer-fields $$
\sqrt{9 - 4 x^{2}}=3\sqrt{1-(\frac{2 x}{3})^2}.

$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{3}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{2}\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{3}{2}\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{2 x}{3} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "dfc32bf8-6ace-5e48-bc5e-92e930371a4c" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "dfc32bf8-6ace-5e48-bc5e-92e930371a4c" :question/answer-fields "9b712a6e-6e52-5783-8e96-8c4185897b37" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "9b712a6e-6e52-5783-8e96-8c4185897b37" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}=3\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{3})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=3\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{4}{3}\cdot 3=4$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=4\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
4\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=4\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
4\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{x}{3} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "9b712a6e-6e52-5783-8e96-8c4185897b37" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "9b712a6e-6e52-5783-8e96-8c4185897b37" :question/answer-fields $$
\int \frac{3}{\sqrt{25 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "d8bfa756-584c-546f-9389-10257daa4f6d" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{5}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{5})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{25 - x^{2}}=5\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{5})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=5\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{3}{5}\cdot 5=3$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{\sqrt{25 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=3\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
3\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=3\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
3\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{x}{5} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "d8bfa756-584c-546f-9389-10257daa4f6d" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "d8bfa756-584c-546f-9389-10257daa4f6d" :question/answer-fields $$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.

4\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=4\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "ffa9d174-c2fd-5424-b8d2-3acccef9ad99" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{4}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{4})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

$$
\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}=4\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{4})^2}.

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{25 - 4 x^{2}}=5\sqrt{1-(\frac{2 x}{5})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{5}{2}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{4}{5}\cdot \frac{5}{2}=2$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{25 - 4 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{2 x}{5} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "a4759172-33f7-52ee-b4bf-483a956b3b02" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "a4759172-33f7-52ee-b4bf-483a956b3b02" :question/answer-fields $$

$$

$$

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{3}\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{3 x}{2} \right)}\right)+C.

\int \frac{2}{\sqrt{25 - 16 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "5a421a58-948e-5542-a6c4-c105fa219eee" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{4 x}{5}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{4}{5})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{25 - 16 x^{2}}=5\sqrt{1-(\frac{4 x}{5})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{5}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{2}{5}\cdot \frac{5}{4}=\frac{1}{2}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{\sqrt{25 - 16 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{2}\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{4 x}{5} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "5a421a58-948e-5542-a6c4-c105fa219eee" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "5a421a58-948e-5542-a6c4-c105fa219eee" :question/answer-fields Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "e9837837-4dfe-557d-bb99-4d563c43757b" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{4 x}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{4}{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{9 - 16 x^{2}}=3\sqrt{1-(\frac{4 x}{3})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{3}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{4}=\frac{1}{4}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{9 - 16 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{4}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{4}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{4}\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{4}\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{4 x}{3} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "e9837837-4dfe-557d-bb99-4d563c43757b" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "e9837837-4dfe-557d-bb99-4d563c43757b" :question/answer-fields $$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "dfc32bf8-6ace-5e48-bc5e-92e930371a4c" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{2 x}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{2}{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{9 - 4 x^{2}}=3\sqrt{1-(\frac{2 x}{3})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{3}{2}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $1\cdot \frac{3}{2}=\frac{3}{2}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{\sqrt{9 - 4 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{3}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{2}\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{3}{2}\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{2 x}{3} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] [:db/add "dfc32bf8-6ace-5e48-bc5e-92e930371a4c" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "dfc32bf8-6ace-5e48-bc5e-92e930371a4c" :question/answer-fields Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] ["f0d24e1a-b76a-52fa-be50-ddfb085b96e6" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}=2\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{2})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=2\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $1\cdot 2=2$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] ["f0d24e1a-b76a-52fa-be50-ddfb085b96e6" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["f0d24e1a-b76a-52fa-be50-ddfb085b96e6" :question/answer-fields "0928067e-abf1-5601-af9a-eb0232cac731"] ["ef9178db-b6e7-5406-845d-17dcc05cb1b7" :question/id #uuid "ef9178db-b6e7-5406-845d-17dcc05cb1b7"] ["ef9178db-b6e7-5406-845d-17dcc05cb1b7" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] ["ef9178db-b6e7-5406-845d-17dcc05cb1b7" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{4}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{4})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}=4\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{4})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=4\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{3}{4}\cdot 4=3$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=3\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
3\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=3\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
3\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{x}{4} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] ["ef9178db-b6e7-5406-845d-17dcc05cb1b7" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["ef9178db-b6e7-5406-845d-17dcc05cb1b7" :question/answer-fields "791b6536-9985-59fa-b96f-2454c13c5270"] Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{4 - 9 x^{2}}=2\sqrt{1-(\frac{3 x}{2})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{2}{3}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{3}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - 9 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{3}\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{3 x}{2} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] ["bae20d5d-4436-5e8e-8143-212aaf8c29ca" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["bae20d5d-4436-5e8e-8143-212aaf8c29ca" :question/answer-fields "6ed717e7-eac0-5f19-899d-85290b2c76c1"] :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{3}{\sqrt{9 - 4 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] ["dfc32bf8-6ace-5e48-bc5e-92e930371a4c" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{2 x}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{2}{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{9 - 4 x^{2}}=3\sqrt{1-(\frac{2 x}{3})^2}.
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{3}{2}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $1\cdot \frac{3}{2}=\frac{3}{2}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{\sqrt{9 - 4 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{3}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{2}\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{3}{2}\left(\arcsin{\left(\frac{2 x}{3} \right)}\right)+C.
$$"] ["dfc32bf8-6ace-5e48-bc5e-92e930371a4c" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["dfc32bf8-6ace-5e48-bc5e-92e930371a4c" :question/answer-fields "cf293a22-6792-5aaf-9cdc-3621ff704f81"]
